entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3 13-09-2024 Heard Mr. Jeetendra Narayan, learned counsel for the petitioner, Mr. Kumar Praveen representing the informant as also learned APP.

2. The petitioner is in custody in connection with Aurangabad Town P.S. Case No. 129 of 2021 for the offence punishable under sections 420, 406 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code lodged on 05.04.2021 by the informant, Rajesh Kumar Singh.

3. As per the prosecution story, the informant who wanted to run a business relating to aluminum foil container, the petitioner was paid a sum of Rs. 27,60,000/- when he was introduced by co-accused, Pankaj Kumar Sinha and Neeraj Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.41320 of 2024(3)
dt.13-09-2024 Kumar Sinha but the machine never reached the place of the informant which led to the FIR.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there are certain facts which include the receipt of the money which cannot be ignored but the fact remains that he in turn made payment from the place where it was to come but they defaulted which resulted into his implication.
It is his further submission that he being the sole bread earner, the father is no more, only after he comes out will be able to start making payment to the informant 5.
Learned counsel for the informant submits that if the petitioner intends to make payment, he has no objection of him being granted interim relief.
6. In that background, this Court deems it appropriate that the petitioner is granted provisional bail of two months as he has already undertaken to start making payment to the informant.

7. Let the petitioner be released on provisional bail for a period two months on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Ten thousand) each with two sureties of like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Aurangabad, in connection with Aurangabad Town P.S. Case No.
129 of 2021 Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.41320 of 2024(3) dt.13-09-2024 subject to the following conditions:
(i) one of the bailor should be the family member/relative of the petitioner who shall provide official document to show his/her bona fide.
(ii) the petitioners shall in no way try to induce or promise or threat the witnesses or tamper with the evidences, failing which the State shall be at liberty to take steps for cancellation of the bail bonds;
(iii) the petitioners shall desist from committing any criminal offence again, failing which the State shall be at liberty to take steps for cancellation of their bail bonds.
8. List this case on 25.10.2024.
(Rajiv Roy, J) Adnan/-
